messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
For a projectile launched with speed \(v\) at an angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal, the horizontal component of the velocity is \(v_x = v\cos\theta\).  
If the launch is in a uniform gravitational field and we ignore air resistance, the horizontal distance travelled after a time \(t\) is simply

\[
\boxed{d(t)=v\cos\theta \; t}
\]

So, for example, if you launch a car at \(v=20\;\text{m/s}\) at \(\theta=30^\circ\) and let it run for \(t=5\;\text{s}\), the horizontal distance would be

\[
d = 20\cos30^\circ \times 5 \approx 86.6\;\text{m}.
\]

If you want the total distance travelled along the trajectory (i.e., the arc length), that would require integrating the speed over time, which depends on the vertical component and gravity. For the simple horizontal range, the formula above suffices.
